quickAnswer: Enter Ihlara Valley at the main Ihlara (380-step) Gate and walk 4 km downstream along the Melendiz River to Belisırma for frescoed Byzantine chapels, or start at Ihlara Village for a quieter 7 km hike. Your €15 ticket (2026) also includes Selime Monastery 10 minutes north; plan 75–85 minutes each way by road from Göreme.

body.text: Which entrance (Ihlara Village vs Belisırma) gives the nicest 4–7 km river walk?

For the most rewarding 4 km walk, enter at the main Ihlara Valley Gate (380 stone stairs down into the canyon), visit the concentrated Byzantine fresco churches (Ağaçaltı, Sümbüllü, and Yılanlı), and hike flat downstream beside the Melendiz River to Belisırma Village. Starting further upstream in Ihlara Village stretches the walk to roughly 7 km with fewer crowds.

body.text: Official 2026 admission to [Ihlara Valley](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-ekle?catalogNo=WEB-IH101-87-009) is €15 for foreign visitors (or covered by the €65 3-day [MuseumPass Cappadocia](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-19-009)), with winter hours typically 08:30–17:00 and last entry at 16:15 ([Cappadocia Travel Guide](https://turkeyitineraries.com/destinations/cappadocia/)). If you are self-driving without a pickup driver, park directly at Belisırma Village, walk 2.5 km upstream to the main fresco chapels, and stroll back to your car without climbing the 380-step staircase.
How do you pair the gorge walk with Selime rock-cut Monastery?

Hold onto your €15 Ihlara Valley ticket stub—it also grants same-day entry to [Selime Monastery](https://goremecityguide.com/ihlara-valley/), located just 7 km (10 minutes by car) north of Belisırma at the canyon's dramatic exit. Hike the gorge in the morning, eat lunch in Belisırma, and climb Selime's multi-story rock-cut cathedral in the softer early-afternoon light.

Carved into volcanic tuff between the 8th and 13th centuries, Selime is the largest rock-cut monastic complex in Cappadocia, containing a basilica-plan cathedral, vaulted kitchen with soot-darkened chimney, stables, and defensive tunnels. The climb up loose sandy rock paths takes 40 to 50 minutes round-trip and requires grippy footwear. Pair this southern excursion with an early stop at Kaymaklı or Derinkuyu Underground City (€13, open from 08:00) ([Cappadocia Travel Guide](https://turkeyitineraries.com/destinations/cappadocia/)) so you cover all major southern sights in one clean loop.
Where do you eat riverside trout lunch in Belisırma?

Belisırma Village sits right on the Melendiz River at the 4 km trail exit, lined with family-run restaurants featuring wooden dining platforms built directly over the rushing water. Order fresh grilled rainbow trout (alabalık) or clay-pot stews (güveç) at spots such as Aslan Restaurant or Star Restaurant, sitting barefoot on cushioned riverside decks.
To keep lunch relaxed and avoid tour-bus crowds, follow this simple checklist:

items: Arrive before 12:30 or after 14:15: Shared Green Tour minibuses pack Belisırma's riverside decks between 12:45 and 14:00.
Check menu prices upfront: Ask for a printed menu before ordering grilled trout, mezze, or fresh-squeezed pomegranate juice.

Bring light layers in spring and autumn: Shaded canyon water stays noticeably cooler than the open Göreme plateau—review our [Türkiye winter travel guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide) if visiting between November and March.
Wear closed-toe trail shoes: Riverbanks near Belisırma and the steep tuff slopes at Selime get slippery in sandals.
Carry small Turkish lira notes: Trailside tea stands and village parking attendants often prefer cash over cards.

body.text: How long is the drive from Göreme (75 min)?

The direct drive from Göreme to the Ihlara Valley Main Gate covers roughly 80 to 85 km via Nevşehir and Derinkuyu, taking 75 to 85 minutes each way in normal daylight traffic. If you stop at Derinkuyu Underground City en route (40 minutes from Göreme), expect another 40 minutes from Derinkuyu to the canyon rim.

Leaving Göreme at 08:00 puts you at Derinkuyu at 08:40, at Ihlara's Main Gate by 10:30, at a quiet Belisırma riverside table by 12:15, and at Selime Monastery by 14:00—returning you to Göreme well before sunset without rushing. If you are building a wider Anatolian road trip beyond Cappadocia, explore our [Bursa destination guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/bursa) for historic stops further west.

faq.q: Does the €15 Ihlara Valley ticket include Selime Monastery?
faq.a: Yes. Keep your paper or digital ticket after exiting Ihlara Valley—the single €15 foreign-visitor ticket covers both the canyon churches and the Selime Monastery entrance on the same day.

faq.q: Can you walk all the way from Ihlara Valley to Selime Monastery?
faq.a: Yes, the full gorge from Ihlara Village to Selime is roughly 14 km (4–5 hours), though the stretch north of Belisırma has fewer frescoed chapels and less shade than the central 4 km section.

faq.q: Is the Ihlara Valley hike difficult for older travelers or children?
faq.a: The riverside path itself is flat and shaded, making it easy for most ages. The main physical hurdle is the 380-step staircase at the Main Gate, which you can bypass entirely by entering directly at Belisırma Village.

faq.q: Are there restrooms and tea stops inside Ihlara Valley?
faq.a: Yes. Basic restrooms sit at the Main Gate, at the midpoint riverside tea garden near the canyon's wooden footbridges, and at all riverside restaurants in Belisırma Village.

faq.q: Is Selime Monastery safe to climb in wet weather?
faq.a: Be cautious after rain or snow: the smooth volcanic tuff slopes at Selime become slick when wet, so wear lugged hiking shoes and skip the steepest upper ledges during heavy rain.

faq.q: Is public transit practical from Göreme to Ihlara Valley?
faq.a: Not for a single-day trip. Public minibuses require multiple transfers via Nevşehir and Aksaray, eating half the day; a rental car or private driver is far more practical.
